summary: Independent read-only compatibility verification accepted the final verifier and unchanged oracle on local Windows Python 3.10.0 and 3.11.9. Targeted and full suites, eight legacy-package commands, complete executed mutation assertions, exact-case behavior, and an intermediate-junction probe all passed without repository or package changes. Real os.symlink execution, Linux, and every GitHub Actions matrix cell remain pending rather than passed.

claims.claim: The independently reviewed verifier and accepted oracle retained their committed identities.
evidence: git diff --exit-code 1597daa for those two paths returned 0.
Pre-run and post-run git status were exactly the clean feature/v0.4-portable-integrity branch.

claims.claim: Every contract-required local test and legacy-package command passed on Python 3.10 and 3.11.
evidence: Python 3.10 targeted 14 and full 58 tests passed; each run skipped the same combined real-symlink method; exits 0.
Python 3.11 targeted 14 and full 58 tests passed; each run skipped the same combined real-symlink method; exits 0.
Four verify_integrity.py and four validate_evidence.py legacy-package commands exited 0 with empty stdout.

claims.claim: The executed mutation corpus was exact, repeatable, and read-only.
evidence: All executed mutation assertions compared complete expected and actual finding sets and passed on both runtimes.
The accepted helper ran validations twice and compared full pre/post temporary-package snapshots.
Unsafe paths patched Path.open to reject every out-of-package open; no boundary assertion fired.
Injected manifest, inventory, listed-file, and read-boundary failures produced stable repeated findings.

claims.claim: Independent Windows probes confirmed case-sensitive serialized lookup and no-follow behavior for intermediate junctions.
evidence: case.txt versus manifest Case.txt produced MANIFEST_FILE_MISSING Case.txt plus MANIFEST_UNLISTED_FILE case.txt twice with equal package identities.
A junction at linked pointing out of the selected package produced MANIFEST_FILE_NOT_REGULAR linked/target.txt plus MANIFEST_UNSUPPORTED_OBJECT linked twice.
The junction target canary and manifest SHA-256 values were unchanged before/after.
Both automatically cleaned probe roots were removed.

claims.claim: No unresolved Critical or Required local-scope finding exists.
evidence: Unexecuted platform cells and real os.symlink coverage remain explicit caveats rather than false passing claims.

uncertainty: The combined manifest/listed-file/directory real-os.symlink test method skipped before any of its three assertions on both local runtimes because Windows returned WinError 1314.
Linux Python 3.10 and 3.11 were not executed locally.
GitHub Actions ubuntu-latest/Python 3.10, ubuntu-latest/Python 3.11, windows-latest/Python 3.10, and windows-latest/Python 3.11 were not dispatched or observed.
The checked-in workflow remains the pre-V4-T4 Ubuntu-only GNU sha256sum workflow; this is pending downstream integration, not a V4-T3 defect.
Integrity is relative to a trusted manifest, assumes a quiescent package, and does not establish authenticity or concurrent-adversary safety.
